articles.job_description: Capgemini Engineering, leader mondial des services d'ingénierie, rassemble des équipes d'ingénieurs, de scientifiques et d'architectes pour aider les entreprises les plus innovantes dans le monde à libérer leur potentiel. Des voitures autonomes aux robots qui sauvent des vies, nos experts en technologies digitales et logicielles sortent des sentiers battus en fournissant des services uniques de R&D et d'ingénierie dans tous les secteurs d'activité. Rejoignez-nous pour une carrière pleine d'opportunités, où vous pouvez faire la différence et où aucun jour ne se ressemble. Dans le cadre du développement d’une nouvelle génération d’architectures électriques et électroniques automobiles, nous recherchons un Digital Twin Architecture Engineer qui contribuera à la création et à l’évolution d’un jumeau numérique (Digital Twin) de l’architecture physique EE. Ce Digital Twin permettra de supporter les analyses de partitionnement et d’allocation d’architecture, d’évaluer différents scénarios techniques et de générer des indicateurs d’aide à la décision pour les équipes d’ingénierie véhicule. Le poste implique une forte interaction avec les équipes Architecture, Systems Engineering, Wiring Harness et CAD 3D afin d'assurer la cohérence des données d'architecture et leur exploitation dans les outils de développement. Créer, développer et maintenir le Digital Twin de l’Architecture Électrique et Électronique (EE Physical Architecture) à partir des données existantes Capital Logic, Capital Integrator et Architecture Superset. Assurer la cohérence et la mise à jour automatique du Digital Twin en intégrant les évolutions de l’Architecture Superset. Contribuer aux activités de partitionnement et d’allocation d’architecture en fournissant des analyses comparatives et des indicateurs de performance (KPIs) pour faciliter la prise de décision. Exploiter les capacités de Capital Integrator pour les échanges de données avec les outils de CAO 3D, notamment pour les informations liées aux faisceaux électriques (longueurs, partitionnement, routage). Développer et automatiser les processus de collecte, transformation et exploitation des données à l’aide de Python et d’outils de traitement de données. Participer à la définition et à l’amélioration des modèles d’architecture dans une approche Systems Engineering / MBSE . Produire les KPIs d’architecture et réaliser les analyses de compromis (trade-off analysis) afin d’orienter les décisions techniques. Collaborer avec les équipes Architecture, Systèmes, Développement et CAO pour garantir la cohérence des données et des modèles. Assurer la documentation technique et la communication des résultats auprès des différentes parties prenantes du projet. Travailler conformément aux processus et standards de développement du Client. Bac+5 en Génie Électrique, Électronique, Systèmes Embarqués, Informatique Industrielle ou équivalent. Profil confirmé : 3 à 5 ans d’expérience en architecture E/E, ingénierie systèmes, développement automobile ou Digital Twin. Compétences techniques – Priorités : Priorité 1 (impérative) Bonne maîtrise de l’ architecture électrique et électronique automobile : ECU, ZCU, IO Aggregators, capteurs, actionneurs, câblage et architecture véhicule. Excellente connaissance de Capital Logic et Capital Integrator . Expérience dans l’échange de données entre Capital Integrator et les outils de CAO 3D . Compétences avancées en Python , automatisation et traitement de données. Connaissance des cycles de développement automobile. Compréhension des concepts de Systems Engineering / MBSE (allocation, interfaces, modélisation d’architecture). Expérience dans le développement de KPIs techniques et l’analyse de compromis (Trade-off Analysis). Connaissance des architectures Brain Vehicle et des stratégies de partitionnement. Expérience en modélisation et gestion de données complexes d’architecture. Connaissance des faisceaux électriques et de leur intégration 3D. Excellentes capacités d’analyse et de résolution de problèmes complexes. Esprit de synthèse et orientation résultats. Autonomie et rigueur dans la gestion des activités techniques. Capacité à travailler dans un environnement multiculturel et multidisciplinaire. Très bonnes compétences en communication et en documentation technique. Le groupe Capgemini encourage une culture inclusive dans un cadre multiculturel et handi-accueillant. En nous rejoignant, vous intégrez un collectif qui valorise la diversité, développe le potentiel de ses talents, s’engage dans des initiatives solidaires avec ses partenaires, et se mobilise pour réduire son impact environnemental sur tous ses sites et auprès de ses clients. Capgemini est un leader mondial, responsable et multiculturel, regroupant près de 350 000 personnes dans plus de 50 pays. Fort de 55 ans d’expérience, nous sommes un partenaire stratégique des entreprises pour la transformation de leurs activités en tirant profit de toute la puissance de la technologie et des innovations dans les domaines en perpétuelle évolution tels que le cloud, la data, l’Intelligence Artificielle, la connectivité, les logiciels, l’ingénierie digitale ou les plateformes.

Analyse et validation des performances structurelles des véhicules et sous-systèmes. Gestion et validation des PIV numériques en collaboration avec les ingénieurs Performance. Validation et optimisation des calculs BIW (Body-in-White) et Closures. Corrélation des résultats numériques avec les essais physiques. Expertise en calcul de durabilité véhicule et NVH. Maîtrise des outils de simulation numérique : LS-DYNA, NASTRAN, ABAQUS, Radioss, ANSA et META . Bonne connaissance des méthodes de calcul par éléments finis. Maîtrise de l'analyse des résultats et de l'optimisation des performances mécaniques. Connaissance de l'environnement de développement automobile et des processus de validation. Réaliser des simulations numériques de durabilité, vibrations, acoustique et crash. Assurer la validation et l'optimisation des performances des structures BIW et Closures. Participer à la définition des plans de validation numérique et physique. Analyser les résultats de calcul et formaliser les conclusions avec un avis métier argumenté. Collaborer avec les équipes conception pour proposer des solutions d'amélioration et d'optimisation. Assurer la corrélation entre les essais physiques et les simulations numériques. Contribuer à la convergence des performances véhicules en respectant les objectifs qualité, coûts et délais. articles.job_description: Choisir Capgemini, c’est choisir une entreprise où vous serez en mesure de façonner votre carrière selon vos aspirations. Avec le soutien et l'inspiration d'une communauté d’experts dans le monde entier, vous pourrez réécrire votre futur. Rejoignez-nous pour redéfinir les limites de ce qui est possible, contribuer à libérer la valeur de la technologie pour les plus grandes organisations et participer à la construction d’un monde plus durable et inclusif. Au sein de nos équipes projet, vous contribuerez au développement de solutions digitales innovantes pour des clients grands comptes dans les secteurs banque, assurance, énergie et industrie. Vous intégrerez une équipe pluridisciplinaire, organisée en mode Agile, et intervenant sur des projets à fort impact métier. En tant qu’Ingénieure/Ingénieur Data GCP, vous interviendrez dans des missions variées telles que : Concevoir et développer des pipelines de données scalables sur GCP (Dataflow, Dataproc, BigQuery…). Participer à l’architecture et à l’industrialisation des solutions data. Assurer la qualité, la sécurité et la performance des traitements de données. Collaborer avec les équipes Data Science, BI et métier pour répondre aux besoins business. Mettre en place des bonnes pratiques DevOps (CI/CD, monitoring, automatisation). Encadrer techniquement des profils juniors et contribuer à la montée en compétences de l’équipe. Diplômé(e) d’un Bac+5 en informatique ou équivalent. Expérience confirmée (≥ 5 ans) sur un poste similaire. Maîtrise des outils : BigQuery, Dataflow, Dataproc, Pub/Sub, Cloud Storage. Solides compétences en Python, SQL, et éventuellement PySpark. Connaissance des pratiques DevOps (Terraform, Git, Docker, CI/CD). Capacité à travailler en mode agile, esprit d’analyse, autonomie et leadership technique. Qualité de vie au travail : Possibilité de télétravail au Maroc ainsi qu’a l’international et autonomie dans l’organisation de votre quotidien, missions hybrides selon vos préférences. Apprentissage en continu : accédez aux formations et certifications dédiées à votre techno, accompagnement personnalisé et parcours d’intégration structuré. Projets variés et à fort impact : intervenez auprès de grands comptés dans des secteurs diversifiés avec des enjeux métiers et technologiques stimulants. Écosystème d’expertise : bénéficiez d’un accompagnement technique personnalisé et d’une intégration active dans nos communautés métiers. Le groupe Capgemini encourage une culture inclusive dans un cadre multiculturel et handi-accueillant. En nous rejoignant, vous intégrez un collectif qui valorise la diversité, développe le potentiel de ses talents, s’engage dans des initiatives solidaires avec ses partenaires, et se mobilise pour réduire son impact environnemental sur tous ses sites et auprès de ses clients. Capgemini est un leader mondial, responsable et multiculturel, regroupant près de 350 000 personnes dans plus de 50 pays. Fort de 55 ans d’expérience, nous sommes un partenaire stratégique des entreprises pour la transformation de leurs activités en tirant profit de toute la puissance de la technologie et des innovations dans les domaines en perpétuelle évolution tels que le cloud, la data, l’Intelligence Artificielle, la connectivité, les logiciels, l’ingénierie digitale ou les plateformes.

articles.job_description: At Capgemini Engineering, the world leader in engineering services, we bring together a global team of engineers, scientists, and architects to help the world’s most innovative companies unleash their potential. From autonomous cars to life-saving robots, our digital and software technology experts think outside the box as they provide unique R&D and engineering services across all industries. Join us for a career full of opportunities. Where you can make a difference. Where no two days are the same. .Organiser et coordonner les opérations de transport international (routier, maritime et aérien). Assurer le suivi des expéditions de l'enlèvement jusqu'à la livraison. Gérer les relations avec les transporteurs, transitaires et partenaires logistiques. Préparer et vérifier les documents de transport et d'export/import. Veiller au respect des réglementations douanières et internationales. Analyser les coûts de transport et proposer des solutions d'optimisation. Traiter les réclamations et résoudre les éventuels incidents liés aux expéditions. Assurer un reporting régulier sur l'activité Bac+5 en Logistique, Transport, Commerce International ou équivalent. Expérience d'au moins 1 an dans le domaine du transport international, de la logistique ou du transit. Bonne maîtrise des Incoterms et des procédures douanières. Maîtrise des outils bureautiques et des logiciels de gestion logistique. Français courant ; l'anglais professionnel est un atout. Sens de l'organisation, rigueur et excellent relationnel. Capacité à gérer plusieurs dossiers simultanément dans un environnement dynamique. Capgemini is a global business and technology transformation partner, helping organizations to accelerate their dual transition to a digital and sustainable world, while creating tangible impact for enterprises and society. It is a responsible and diverse group of 340,000 team members in more than 50 countries. With its strong over 55-year heritage, Capgemini is trusted by its clients to unlock the value of technology to address the entire breadth of their business needs. It delivers end-to-end services and solutions leveraging strengths from strategy and design to engineering, all fueled by its market leading capabilities in AI, generative AI, cloud and data, combined with its deep industry expertise and partner ecosystem.

articles.job_description: Explore our current job opportunities National Consultant on Youth Ecosystem Mapping and Youth Engagement Apply now Job no: 595918 Contract type: Consultant Duty Station: Ashkhabad Level: Consultancy Location: Turkmenistan Categories: Adolescent Development, Social and Behavior Change UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children’s lives, defend their rights, and help them fulfill their potential, from early childhood through adolescence. At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling. UNICEF is a place where careers are built. We offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture., coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package. Visit our website to learn more about what we do at UNICEF. For every child, the right to survival and development UNICEF Turkmenistan is implementing its Country Programme of Cooperation for 2026–2030, which is aligned with national development priorities, the National Action Plan for the Realization of Children's Rights in Turkmenistan (2023–2028), the Sustainable Development Goals and the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework. (UNICEF) The Country Programme identifies climate action and youth as one of its three flagship areas and aims to strengthen climate resilience through education and meaningful youth engagement, recognizing young people as agents of change. (UNICEF) Recent UNICEF-supported initiatives, including the Youth Climate Summer School, have demonstrated both the growing interest of young people in leadership and community action and the value of building nationwide networks of engaged youth. The 2026 programme brought together young people from across all regions and supported the development of youth-led community initiatives. (UNICEF) At the same time, there is a need for a more systematic understanding of the broader youth ecosystem in Turkmenistan. Information on existing youth initiatives, volunteer networks, youth interests, capacities, opportunities and regional differences is fragmented. A consolidated evidence base would support UNICEF and national partners in designing more inclusive, relevant and geographically balanced opportunities for young people. UNICEF therefore seeks to engage a national consultant to conduct a comprehensive mapping of the youth ecosystem in Turkmenistan and develop practical tools and recommendations to strengthen youth participation, volunteering, leadership and youth-led action. How can you make a difference? The purpose of the consultancy is to develop a comprehensive and practical evidence base on the youth ecosystem in Turkmenistan to inform UNICEF's programming and partnerships related to youth participation, leadership, volunteering, climate action and community engagement. The consultancy will identify and map: Existing youth initiatives and youth-led activities across the country; Youth interests, priorities, skills, aspirations and areas of engagement; Existing professional, personal and volunteering network opportunities available to young people and gaps in access to such opportunities; Key institutions, organizations and stakeholders working with and for young people; Database for UNICEF engagement of youth across subjects and initiatives. The consultant will undertake field missions to all regions of Turkmenistan, subject to UNICEF-approved travel plans and in coordination with relevant national and local partners. Travel will support direct consultations with young people, youth groups, institutions and other relevant stakeholders to ensure geographically representative findings. Based on the findings, the consultant will develop practical recommendations and tools to support a more systematic, inclusive and sustainable approach to youth engagement. For the purposes of this assignment, the term “youth” shall be understood in accordance with the Law of Turkmenistan “On State Youth Policy” (Türkmenistanyň Kanuny «Ýaşlar barada döwlet syýasaty hakynda») as citizens of Turkmenistan aged from 14 to 35 years, as defined in Article 1, paragraph 3 of the Law. To qualify as an advocate for every child you will have… Social sciences; Youth development; Education; Public policy; Sociology; Psychology; International development; Or another relevant field. At least 3 years of relevant professional experience in youth development, participation, community engagement, research, programme development or related fields; Experience in qualitative and quantitative research and consultations; Experience in stakeholder mapping and consultation processes; Experience developing databases, mapping tools or analytical reports would be an asset; Experience working with young people: Knowledge of youth-related institutions and the context in Turkmenistan; Experience working across regions and engaging diverse communities; Experience with UNICEF, United Nations or international development organizations would be an asset; Strong facilitation and communication skills; Strong analytical and report-writing skills; Ability to translate findings into practical programme recommendations. Fluency in Turkmen and Russian (spoken and written) is required. Working knowledge of English is an asset. For every Child, you demonstrate... UNICEF’s Core Values of Care, Respect, Integrity, Trust and Accountability and Sustainability (CRITAS) underpin everything we do and how we do it. Get acquainted with Our Values Charter: UNICEF Values The UNICEF competencies required for this post are… (1) Builds and maintains partnerships (2) Demonstrates self-awareness and ethical awareness (3) Drive to achieve results for impact (4) Innovates and embraces change (5) Manages ambiguity and complexity (6) Thinks and acts strategically (7) Works collaboratively with others Familiarize yourself with our competency framework and its different levels. UNICEF promotes and advocates for the protection of the rights of every child, everywhere, in everything it does and is mandated to support the realization of the rights of every child, including those most disadvantaged, and our global workforce must reflect the diversity of those children. The UNICEF family is committed to include everyone, irrespective of their race/ethnicity, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, nationality, socio-economic background, minority, or any other status. UNICEF encourages applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender, nationality, religious or ethnic backgrounds, and from people with disabilities, including neurodivergence. We offer a wide range of benefits to our staff, including paid parental leave, breastfeeding breaks and reasonable accommodation for persons with disabilities. UNICEF provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process. If you require any accommodation, please submit your request through the accessibility email button on the UNICEF Careers webpage Accessibility | UNICEF. Should you be shortlisted, please get in touch with the recruiter directly to share further details, enabling us to make the necessary arrangements in advance. UNICEF does not hire candidates who are married to children (persons under 18). UNICEF has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and UNICEF, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, fraud, corruption and other forms of misconduct. UNICEF is committed to promoting the protection and safeguarding of all children. All selected candidates will undergo rigorous reference, safeguarding and background verification checks. These checks may include verification of academic credentials and employment history, screening against relevant United Nations misconduct databases, and requests for misconduct disclosures from current and former employers, professional associations, other relevant organizations and participating organizations under inter-agency safeguarding initiatives, including the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme (MDS), where applicable. Appointment, selection and continued engagement are subject to the satisfactory completion of all required checks. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information and consent to enable UNICEF to undertake these checks. Background checks will include the verification of academic credential(s) and employment history. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information to conduct a background check, and selected candidates with disabilities may be requested to submit supporting documentation in relation to their disability confidentially UNICEF appointments are subject to medical clearance. Issuance of a visa by the host country of the duty station is required for IP positions and will be facilitated by UNICEF. Appointments are conditional on the selected candidates’ willingness to comply with current or future vaccination requirements, should UNICEF mandate it for personnel. Failure to comply with such requirements, where applicable and without a duly approved medical exemption from the relevant UN authority, will result in the cancellation of the selection or may lead to other administrative measures, including separation from service As per Article 101, paragraph 3, of the Charter of the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the employment of the staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence, and integrity. UNICEF is committed to fostering an inclusive, representative, and welcoming workforce. Government employees who are considered for employment with UNICEF are normally required to resign from their government positions before taking up an assignment with UNICEF. UNICEF reserves the right to withdraw an offer of appointment, without compensation, if a visa or medical clearance is not obtained, or necessary inoculation requirements are not met, within a reasonable period for any reason. UNICEF does not charge a processing fee at any stage of its recruitment, selection, and hiring processes (i.e., application stage, interview stage, validation stage, or appointment and training). UNICEF will not ask for applicants’ bank account information. Humanitarian action is a cross-cutting priority within UNICEF’s Strategic Plan. UNICEF is committed to stay and deliver in humanitarian contexts. Therefore, all staff, at all levels across all functional areas, can be called upon to be deployed to support humanitarian response, contributing to both strengthening resilience of communities and capacity of national authorities. All UNICEF positions are advertised, and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and advance to the next stage of the selection process. An internal candidate performing at the level of the post in the relevant functional area, or an internal/external candidate in the corresponding Talent Group, may be selected, if suitable for the post, without assessment of other candidates. articles.job_description: Explore our current job opportunities Security Manager, (P-4), FT, #107113, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, ESAR, (For Non-Ethiopian Nationals only) Apply now Job no: 595959 Contract type: Fixed Term Appointment Duty Station: Addis Ababa Location: Ethiopia Categories: Security UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children’s lives, defend their rights, and help them fulfill their potential, from early childhood through adolescence. At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling. UNICEF is a place where careers are built: we offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package. Visit our website to learn more about what we do at UNICEF. For every child, the right to Safety How can you make a difference? UNICEF Ethiopia works to advance the rights and well-being of every child, with a particular focus on the most vulnerable and disadvantaged populations. Operating in a dynamic and complex environment, the Country Office delivers life-saving and developmental programmes across the country. The Security Manager plays a critical role in enabling safe and effective programme implementation by leading security risk management, advising senior management, and supporting personnel, assets, and operations throughout Ethiopia The Security Manager reports to the Country Representative and maintains a direct technical reporting line to the Regional Security Adviser under UNICEF’s matrix-management arrangements. The Security Manager advises and supports the Representative in discharging their security responsibilities in accordance with the United Nations Security Management System and the UNICEF Security Framework of Accountability. On behalf of the Representative, the Security Manager leads and manages security activities in support of UNICEF personnel and eligible family members, premises, assets, programmes and operations throughout Ethiopia, while providing independent security advice to the Representative and Country Management Team. The Representative retains accountability for security matters within the Country Office. Key Roles and Responsibilities 1. Security Risk Management and Planning Serve as the principal security adviser to the Representative and provide strategic advice to Country Management Team (CMT) on security risks and responsibilities. Support and review Security Risk Management (SRM) processes, including specific ad hoc assessments where required; advise the Representative on UNICEF’s position regarding proposed security risk-management measures; and manage the implementation and monitoring of measures approved through the applicable UNSMS decision-making arrangements. Assist UNDSS as appropriate, participate as a member of the Security Cell, and attend Security Management Team and Area Security Management Team meetings as an observer, as applicable. Ensure that UNICEF-specific operational and programme considerations are appropriately presented, while recognizing that the Representative remains UNICEF’s member of the Security Management Team. Lead the implementation and monitoring of approved security risk management measures (SRMM), UNICEF Security plans including other security related preparedness and contingency arrangements across the Country Office and field locations. Maintain required security documentation, incident reporting, and compliance monitoring. Monitor and analyze security risks affecting personnel, assets, and programmes. Oversee security operations and risk management across duty stations. Ensure personnel receive security updates, training, and emergency guidance. Manage security communications and emergency response systems. Conduct residential security assessments and oversee security contractors. Lead and manage the Country Office security function including the supervision, performance management, development and technical oversight of security personnel supporting the main office and field locations. 3. Programmatic Security Information and Analysis Provide forward looking security analysis and advice to enable programme implementation, humanitarian access and informed management decision-making. Ensure that security risk considerations are integrated into programme strategy, planning, field delivery, emergency preparedness, business continuity and operational decision-making. Advise programme and operations teams on practical risk management options that support principled presence, access and delivery in high-risk as well as hard-to-reach locations. 4. Security Networking and Partnership Building Maintain partnerships with UN, NGO, diplomatic, and local security counterparts. . Represent UNICEF in relevant inter-agency security forums and maintain effective coordination with UNDSS, members of the security cell, United Nations Entities and other security counterparts. Maintain a direct technical reporting line to the Regional Security Adviser, regular technical coordination with the Office of Security Coordination (OSC) and timely operational reporting to OPSCEN on significant incidents and developments in accordance with applicable reporting requirements. Strengthen security collaboration with implementing partners under the Saving Lives Together (SLT) framework. 5. Security Compliance Monitoring Monitor compliance with security policies, procedures, and risk mitigation measures. Review security proposals, budgets, and documentation, providing technical advice as needed. Advise the Representative on identified security compliance gaps, residual risks, required corrective measures and any matters requiring management decision and/or escalation. Monitor the implementation of agreed corrective actions and provide periodic compliance updates to the Representative and RSA 6. Innovation, Knowledge Management and Capacity Building Promote innovative security systems and practices. Capture and share lessons learned and best practices. Lead security training and capacity-building initiatives. Brief managers on UN security policies, tools, and guidelines. Ensure inclusive, gender- and disability-sensitive training programmes. If you would like to know more about this position, please review the complete Job Description here: GJP - Security Manager Level 4.pdf To qualify as an advocate for every child you will have… Education: Master or equivalent (Advanced University Degree) in security risk management, International Studies, Political Science, international relations, intelligence studies, peace and conflict studies, diplomatic studies, counterterrorism and any other related fields is required. A first-level university degree in a relevant field, in combination with ten years of qualifying experience, may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. Work Experience: At least eight (08) years of progressively responsible professional experience in security risk management, security analysis, is required. Demonstrated international security-management experience in emergency and/or conflict affected contexts and an understanding of the United Nations Security Management System is required. Skills: Demonstrated ability to provide strategic security advice, lead security risk management processes, produce high quality security analysis and reporting, coordinate with inter-agency security arrangements, manage emergency preparedness and response and lead security personnel in complex operational environments is required. Language Requirements: Fluency in English is required. Knowledge of another official UN language (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian or Spanish) or a local language is an asset. Experience in developing country and emergency operations settings, including conflict zones, with a strong track record of interagency security coordination to support safe and effective humanitarian and development programmes are considered an asset. Relevant experience at country level, particularly in development, fragile settings and humanitarian contexts. For every Child, you demonstrate... UNICEF's Core Values of Care, Respect, Integrity, Trust and Accountability and Sustainability (CRITAS) underpin everything we do and how we do it. Get acquainted with Our Values Charter: UNICEF Values UNICEF competencies required for this post are… Nurtures, Leads and Manages People (Level 2) Demonstrates Self Awareness and Ethical Awareness (Level 2) Works Collaboratively with others (Level 2) Builds and Maintains Partnerships (Level 2) Innovates and Embraces Change (Level 2) Thinks and Acts Strategically (Level 2) Drive to achieve impactful results (Level 2) Manages ambiguity and complexity (Level 2) Familiarize yourself with our competency framework and their different levels. UNICEF promotes and advocates for the protection of the rights of every child, everywhere, in everything it does and is mandated to support the realization of the rights of every child, including those most disadvantaged, and our global workforce must reflect the diversity of those children. The UNICEF family is committed to include everyone, irrespective of their race/ethnicity, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, nationality, socio-economic background, minority, or any other status. UNICEF encourages applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender, nationality, religious or ethnic backgrounds, and from people with disabilities, including neurodivergence. We offer a wide range of benefits to our staff, including paid parental leave, breastfeeding breaks and reasonable accommodation for persons with disabilities. UNICEF provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process. If you require any accommodation, please submit your request through the accessibility email button on the UNICEF Careers webpage Accessibility | UNICEF. Should you be shortlisted, please get in touch with the recruiter directly to share further details, enabling us to make the necessary arrangements in advance. UNICEF does not hire candidates who are married to children (persons under 18). UNICEF has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and UNICEF, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, fraud, corruption and other forms of serious misconduct. UNICEF is committed to promoting the protection and safeguarding of all children. All selected candidates will undergo rigorous reference, safeguarding and background verification checks. These checks may include verification of academic credentials and employment history, screening against relevant United Nations misconduct databases, and requests for misconduct disclosures from current and former employers, professional associations, other relevant organizations and participating organizations under inter-agency safeguarding initiatives, including the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme (MDS), where applicable. Appointment, selection and continued engagement are subject to the satisfactory completion of all required checks. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information and consent to enable UNICEF to undertake these checks. Background checks will include the verification of academic credential(s) and employment history. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information to conduct a background check, and selected candidates with disabilities may be requested to submit supporting documentation in relation to their disability confidentially. UNICEF appointments are subject to medical clearance. Issuance of a visa by the host country of the duty station is required for IP positions and will be facilitated by UNICEF. Appointments are conditional on the selected candidates willingness to comply with current or future vaccination requirements, should UNICEF mandate it for personnel. Failure to comply with such requirements, where applicable and without a duly approved medical exemption from the relevant UN authority, will result in the cancellation of the selection or may lead to other administrative measures, including separation from service. As per Article 101, paragraph 3, of the Charter of the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the employment of the staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence, and integrity. UNICEF is committed to fostering an inclusive, representative, and welcoming workforce. For this position, eligible and suitable Females are encouraged to apply. Government employees who are considered for employment with UNICEF are normally required to resign from their government positions before taking up an assignment with UNICEF. UNICEF reserves the right to withdraw an offer of appointment, without compensation, if a visa or medical clearance is not obtained, or necessary inoculation requirements are not met, within a reasonable period for any reason. UNICEF does not charge a processing fee at any stage of its recruitment, selection, and hiring processes (i.e., application stage, interview stage, validation stage, or appointment and training). UNICEF will not ask for applicants' bank account information. Mobility is a condition of international professional employment with UNICEF and an underlying premise of the international civil service. Humanitarian action is a cross-cutting priority within UNICEF's Strategic Plan. UNICEF is committed to stay and deliver in humanitarian contexts. Therefore, all staff, at all levels across all functional areas, can be called upon to be deployed to support humanitarian response, contributing to both strengthening resilience of communities and capacity of national authorities. All UNICEF positions are advertised, and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and advance to the next stage of the selection process. An internal candidate performing at the level of the post in the relevant functional area, or an internal/external candidate in the corresponding Talent Group, may be selected, if suitable for the post, without assessment of other candidates. Additional information about working for UNICEF can be found here. Advertised: 01 Oct 2026 E. Africa Standard Time Deadline: 08 Oct 2026 E. The role provides expert security advice, oversees security operations and compliance, strengthens partnerships, and enables safe and effective programme delivery across a complex operating environment. The ideal incumbent will have an advanced degree in security, international relations, conflict analysis, or a related field, and at least eight years of international security management experience. articles.job_description: Explore our current job opportunities Social & Behaviour Change Specialist (NO-3), FT, #00137825, Kathmandu - Nepal, APR (Open only for Nepalese Nationals) Apply now Job no: 596010 Contract type: Fixed Term Appointment Duty Station: Kathmandu Location: Nepal Categories: Social and Behavior Change UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children’s lives, defend their rights, and help them fulfill their potential, from early childhood through adolescence. At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling. UNICEF is a place where careers are built: we offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package. Visit our website to learn more about what we do at UNICEF. For every child, the right to a Champion How can you make a difference? UNICEF Nepal is strengthening its Social & Behavioural Change (SBC) agenda to accelerate sustainable results for children and adolescents. Through systems strengthening for supportive public plans and policies, applied behavioural science for norms-shifting, and SBC+ ecosystem for expression and participation (Risk Communication, Community Engagement and Accountability to Affected Populations approaches), the position will help shape policies, influence social norms, promote participation, and enhance public sector capacity to deliver behaviourally informed and inclusive services. As the Social and Behaviour Change (SBC) Specialist, you will provide strategic leadership in applying behavioural science, social research, data analytics, and community engagement to address persistent inequities, strengthen systems, and improve outcomes for children. You will lead the design and implementation of innovative, evidence-driven, and multi-sectoral SBC+ strategies that influence policies, services, social norms, and individual behaviours across development and humanitarian contexts. Working closely with government, communities, partners, and UNICEF programme teams, you will champion people-centred approaches that strengthen accountability, amplify community voices, and enhance preparedness, resilience, and recovery in the face of climate, disaster, and humanitarian challenges. You will also lead the SBC team, drive organizational learning and innovation, and support the institutionalization of sustainable SBC+ approaches within national and sub-national systems, positioning UNICEF Nepal as a leader in evidence-based Social and Behavior Change. The key functions/accountabilities includes: 1. Providing strategic and technical leadership in applied behavioural science, ensuring robust social and behavioural evidence informs policies, systems strengthening and SBC programming across development and humanitarian contexts. 2. Serving as the technical anchor for SBC data, measurement, monitoring and learning, translating evidence into accountable, adaptive and results-oriented programming. 3. Leading the design and quality assurance of integrated, multisectoral SBC strategies, ensuring behavioural insights are effectively converted into inclusive, sustainable programme interventions. 4. Championing innovation and digital SBC approaches, leveraging technology and behavioural insights to enhance scale, efficiency and impact while managing ethical and data-related risks. 5. Strengthening community engagement, participation and accountability systems, ensuring community voices meaningfully inform programme design, implementation and adaptive management. 6. Advancing SBC through strategic advocacy, partnerships and resource mobilization, positioning SBC as a core accelerator within national systems and UNICEF programmes. 7. Building institutional and partner capacity for SBC and systems strengthening, supporting sustainability, preparedness and resilience through skills development and learning. 8. Ensuring effective operational coordination and technical oversight, including supervision of consultants and partners, to deliver coherent, high-quality SBC results across sectors. If you would like to know more about this position, please review the complete Job Description here: JD_Social & Behavior Change Specialist, NO-3, FT.pdf To qualify as an advocate for every child, you will have… Education : An advanced university degree (Master's) in social and behavioural science, including sociology, anthropology, communication studies/communication for development, psychology and/or related field is required. A minimum of five (5) years of relevant progressively responsible professional experience at the national and international levels in developing, implementing, evaluating, and managing Social and Behavior Change strategies and content is required. Demonstrated expertise in the application of social and behaviour change science, theories, research, and analysis, to all stages of the programme cycle. Proven ability to manage social research, including quantitative, qualitative, and participatory methods for formative assessments, identifying behavioural drivers, and tracking, measurement, and evaluation of social change. Demonstrated ability to stay current with new developments in the SBC+ field is required. Familiarity with new and emerging approaches such as behavioural insights, human-centred design and social listening is also required. Demonstrated experience in the execution of complex priorities, processes and projects in office work plans. At least four years' country programme experience with a multilateral development agency or national NGO in a low- or middle-income setting. Proven ability to work with internal and external stakeholders at multiple levels, including providing technical support and capacity building and establishing/managing external partnerships. Skills : Familiarity with Behavioural Science, Social & Behaviour Change (SBC), Strategic Leadership, Community Engagement, Social Research, Behavioural Insights, Human-Centred Design, Monitoring & Evaluation, Evidence-Based Programming, Policy Advocacy, Partnership Development, Capacity Building, Resource Mobilization, Team Leadership, Emergency & Resilience Programming, Data Analytics, and Multi-Sectoral Coordination. Language Requirements : Proficiency in English and Nepali are required. Demonstrated experience in designing, planning and implementing SBC activities informed by global, regional and national social and behavioural evidence, in coordination with multiple sectors. Proven track record of setting strategic and policy direction and leading the development, implementation and monitoring of SBC strategies. Demonstrated experience in monitoring programme funds and resources and ensuring compliance with organizational guidelines, rules and regulations. Experience in fundraising, resource mobilization and partnership development to support SBC programmes and activities. Experience leading and supervising teams to generate and apply research, data and evidence to inform SBC programme design, measurement and monitoring in both development and emergency contexts. Proven experience developing partnerships with academia and learning institutions to deliver SBC capacity-development activities. Relevant country-level experience, particularly in development, fragile and humanitarian contexts. For every Child, you demonstrate... UNICEF's Core Values of Care, Respect, Integrity, Trust and Accountability and Sustainability (CRITAS) underpin everything we do and how we do it. Get acquainted with Our Values Charter: UNICEF Values The UNICEF competencies required for this post are… (1) Builds and maintains partnerships (2) Demonstrates self-awareness and ethical awareness (3) Drive to achieve results for impact (4) Innovates and embraces change (5) Manages ambiguity and complexity (6) Thinks and acts strategically (7) Works collaboratively with others (8) Nurtures, leads and manages people Familiarize yourself with our competency framework and its different levels. This position has been assessed as an elevated-risk role for Child Safeguarding purposes, as it is either a role with direct contact with children, a role that works directly with identifiable children's data, a safeguarding response role, or an assessed risk role. Additional vetting and assessment for elevated risk roles in child safeguarding (potentially including additional criminal background checks) apply. UNICEF promotes and advocates for the protection of the rights of every child, everywhere, in everything it does, and is mandated to support the realization of the rights of every child, including those most disadvantaged; our global workforce must reflect the diversity of those children. The UNICEF family is committed to including everyone, irrespective of their race/ethnicity, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, nationality, socio-economic background, minority, or any other status. UNICEF encourages applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender, nationality, religious or ethnic backgrounds, and from people with disabilities, including neurodivergence. We offer a wide range of benefits to our staff, including paid parental leave, breastfeeding breaks and reasonable accommodation for people with disabilities. UNICEF provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process. If you require any accommodation, please submit your request through the accessibility email button on the UNICEF Careers webpage Accessibility | UNICEF. Should you be shortlisted, please get in touch with the recruiter directly to share further details, enabling us to make the necessary arrangements in advance. UNICEF does not hire candidates who are married to children (persons under 18). UNICEF has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and UNICEF, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities. UNICEF is committed to promoting the protection and safeguarding of all children. All selected candidates will therefore undergo rigorous reference and background checks and will be expected to adhere to these standards and principles. Background checks will include the verification of academic credential(s) and employment history. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information to conduct a background check, and selected candidates with disabilities may be requested to submit supporting documentation in relation to their disability confidentially. UNICEF appointments are subject to medical clearance. Issuance of a visa by the host country of the duty station is required for IP positions and will be facilitated by UNICEF. Appointments are conditional on the selected candidates' willingness to comply with current or future vaccination requirements, should UNICEF mandate it for personnel. Failure to comply with such requirements, where applicable and without a duly approved medical exemption from the relevant UN authority, will result in the cancellation of the selection or may lead to other administrative measures, including separation from service. As per Article 101, paragraph 3, of the Charter of the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the employment of the staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence, and integrity. UNICEF is committed to fostering an inclusive, representative, and welcoming workforce. For this position, eligible and suitable female candidates, candidates from under-represented ethnic groups, and persons with disabilities are encouraged to apply. Government employees who are considered for employment with UNICEF are normally required to resign from their government positions before taking up an assignment with UNICEF. UNICEF reserves the right to withdraw an offer of appointment, without compensation, if a visa or medical clearance is not obtained, or necessary inoculation requirements are not met, within a reasonable period for any reason. UNICEF does not charge a processing fee at any stage of its recruitment, selection, and hiring processes (i.e., application stage, interview stage, validation stage, or appointment and training). UNICEF will not ask for applicants' bank account information. Humanitarian action is a cross-cutting priority within UNICEF's Strategic Plan. UNICEF is committed to stay and deliver in humanitarian contexts. Therefore, all staff, at all levels across all functional areas, can be called upon to be deployed to support humanitarian response, contributing to both strengthening resilience of communities and capacity of national authorities. Visa residence requirements: i.e., UNICEF shall not facilitate the issuance of a visa and work authorization for candidates under consideration for positions in the national officer and general service categories. All UNICEF positions are advertised, and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and advance to the next stage of the selection process. An internal candidate performing at the level of the post in the relevant functional area, or an internal/external candidate in the corresponding Talent Group, may be selected, if suitable for the post, without assessment of other candidates. Additional information about working for UNICEF can be found here. The purpose of this consultancy is to coordinate the implementation of the UNICEF Lao DDR Climate Strategy and prepare activities under the Safe and Clean Environment Outcome of the new Country Programme (2027-2031). This includes, but is not limited to Climate Resilient Social Services, Children Climate Vulnerability and Risk Assessment (CCVRA), Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), Early Warning Systems (EWS), and addressing Air Pollution in Lao PDR. This role will facilitate efficient coordination among various Government stakeholders and development partners, contribute to the implementation of the country programme, and ensure the achievement of programme objectives within stipulated timeframes. The ideal candidate will possess extensive experience and knowledge in project management, government coordination, air quality monitoring, climate- and disaster risk reduction, and climate financing. Lao PDR is highly vulnerable to climate change impacts due to its reliance on climate-sensitive natural resources and low adaptive capacity. The country ranks 16th in the 2026 global Children’s Climate Risk Report, placing children at high risk. Although contributing minimally to global greenhouse gas emissions, Lao PDR is among the world’s most vulnerable and least prepared countries. Inter-sectoral collaboration within UNICEF and with external stakeholders is crucial to address the wide-reaching impacts of climate change. UNICEF Lao PDR is looking for a national coordinator to ensure effective liaison and coordination between the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment (MAE), the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare (MoLSW), the National Designated Authority (NDA), designated line ministries for Education and Health (MoES, MoH), and local governments for the implementation of UNICEF activities. The Consultant will be based at the UNICEF Country Office with in-country field missions, international travel and virtual meetings as needed. At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling. UNICEF is a place where careers are built: we offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package. Visit our website to learn more about what we do at UNICEF. For every child, the right to Education How can you make a difference? Mozambique has one of the youngest populations in the world, with 65 per cent of the population under the age of 24. This demographic profile presents a major opportunity for national development, but only if children, adolescents and young people acquire the foundational, transferable, digital and market-relevant skills needed for further learning, decent work and civic participation. Despite progress in expanding access to education, learning outcomes remain weak, completion rates are low, and many learners leave school without basic literacy and numeracy skills or the competencies required to transition successfully to adulthood. The education system is increasingly overstretched by rapid population growth, limited fiscal space, climate shocks, insecurity and persistent inequities. Schools often lack safe, inclusive and resilient learning environments, sufficient trained teachers, adequate materials and effective accountability systems. The consultant will document promising practices from ASWA III, build the system to generate evidence on WASH impacts across health and education outcomes, support the states to advance on their sustainability response plans, and support the federal government on the HOSI. Key activities that will include: Development of 4 knowledge products documenting progress on climate resilience, sustainability and gender transformative WASH Establishment of indicators and collection of baseline (2024), 2025 and 2026 data of key health and education outcomes from routing government monitoring systems related to WASH, in the ASWA III targeted local government areas (LGA) and communities (Lere and Kagarko LGA in Kaduna, and Shelleng and Ganye LGAs in Adamawa) Support state governments to advance and institutionalize priority actions in the state sustainability plans, and the federal government to develop a concrete activities to be implemented from January 2026 – 2027 in response to the 2021 SWSC. Support the federal government with engagement and initiatives related to HOSI, including: preparations for the UN Water Conference (December 2026), implementation and documentation of 2-3 priority actions from the Nigerian Youth - Government Collaborative Work Plan following the Kigali symposium, and finalization and implementation of the Nigeria Water Compact. The consultancy will also serve a learning and adaptive management function, providing actionable recommendations to strengthen implementation, improve programme effectiveness, and enhance sustainability of ASWA III for the remaining programme period and beyond. If you would like to know more about this consultancy, please review the complete Terms of Reference here: ToR TMC0006744.pdf To qualify as an advocate for every child you will have... ( Qualifications/Experience/ Knowledge/Expertise/Skills) Advanced university degree (Master’s or higher) in one or more of the following fields: Public Health, Community Health, Public Administration, Social Sciences, WASH Engineering, Monitoring and Evaluation, or other closely related disciplines relevant to the assignment. At least 7 years of progressively responsible professional experience in water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) and public health Demonstrated experience in supporting high-level government engagements for international conferences and meetings Proven expertise in Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL), including design and implementation of data management and data collection tools Strong track record in applying evidence and analysis to inform programme design, strategy development, and policy recommendations. Experience in knowledge management, and quantitative and qualitative research methodologies Demonstrated knowledge and experience of supporting sustainability initiatives for WASH services Experience working with government institutions, UN agencies, NGOs, and community stakeholders, particularly in low-resource or development contexts. Excellent facilitation, stakeholder engagement, and communication skills, including ability to interact effectively with diverse audiences at national and local levels. Strong analytical, synthesis, and report writing skills, with ability to produce high-quality, evidence-based outputs within tight deadlines. articles.job_description: خيارات الوصول المرئي متصرف من الدرجة الثانية - سُلمْ 11 الإدارة المنظمة مكتب تنمية التعاون آخر أجل لإيداع الترشيحات 16 أكتوبر 2026 - 16:30 تاريخ إجراء المباراة 22 نونبر 2026 تاريخ النشر 1 أكتوبر 2026 معلومات عن المباراة الدرجة : متصرف من الدرجة الثانية - سُلمْ 11 نوع الإيداع : الإيداع الإلكتروني على الموقع المخصص للإدارة موقع الإيداع : https://www.odco.gov.ma/e-recrutement معلومات إضافية : ترفض طلبات الترشيح غير المسجلة إلكترونيا، وكل ترشيح غيــــر مستوف للوثائق السالفة الذكر أو تم تحميله بطريقة غيـــر صحيحة أو خـــــارج الآجــــــــال لن يــــــؤخـــذ بعــــــيــــــــن الاعتبـــــــار ويحتفظ به دون جواب. سيتم الإعــــــلان عن مكان إجراء المباراة ولائحة المترشحين المقبولين لاجتياز الاختبارات الكتابية والشفوية وكذلك النتائج النهائية للمباراة على الموقع الالكتروني لمكتب تنمية التعاون www.odco.gov.ma وعلى بوابة التشغيل العمومي www.emploi-public.ma. ويعتبر ذلك بمثابة استدعاء للمترشحين المعنيين. هذا الفضاء مخصص لطرح الأسئلة والاستفسارات فقط، وليس لإيداع ملفات الترشيح. تأكيد بواسطة البريد الالكتروني تم إرسال رسالة لتأكيد تسجيل حسابك. يرجى التحقق من رسائل البريد الإلكتروني الخاصة بك

Référence _ Annonce : RH 105/26
L’Office de la Formation Professionnelle et de la Promotion du Travail
lance un Appel à Candidatures pour le poste de :
Formateur en développement digital
(Nombre de Postes : 05)
Descriptif de poste :
Le formateur en développement digital joue un rôle essentiel dans la formation d'une nouvelle génération de
professionnels compétents dans ce domaine en constante évolution, et sa contribution est cruciale pour
répondre aux besoins du marché du travail dans le secteur des nouvelles technologies de l'information.
Le formateur en développement digital occupe un rôle crucial dans le développement des compétences des
stagiaires dans le domaine du développement des nouvelles technologies de l'information. Son objectif
principal est de former une nouvelle génération de professionnels compétents dans le domaine du
développement numérique en leur fournissant les connaissances théoriques et pratiques nécessaires pour
réussir dans ce domaine en constante évolution.
Responsabilités :
• Analyser et interpréter les cahiers des charges pour comprendre les besoins des projets de développement
digital.
• Rédiger des spécifications fonctionnelles et techniques détaillées pour guider le processus de
développement.
• Concevoir et réaliser des maquettes et des prototypes pour visualiser et valider les concepts proposés.
• Concevoir et mettre en place des bases de données pour stocker et gérer efficacement les données.
• Développer des composants logiciels à l'aide de langages de programmation orientés objet tels que Java,
C#, Python, etc.
• Assembler et intégrer les différents composants logiciels pour créer des applications fonctionnelles.
• Réaliser des tests unitaires et des tests d'intégration pour garantir la qualité et la fiabilité des applications
développées.
• Participer à la mise en exploitation des applications et fournir un support technique aux utilisateurs finaux.
• Assurer une veille technologique constante pour rester à jour avec les dernières tendances et technologies
en développement digital.
Compétences requises :
• Excellentes compétences en communication pour transmettre efficacement les connaissances aux
stagiaires.
• Solide expérience pratique dans le développement de logiciels et d'applications digitales.
• Maîtrise des langages de programmation orientés objet et des frameworks associés.
• Capacité à travailler de manière autonome et en équipe.
• Compétences organisationnelles pour planifier et dispenser efficacement les formations.
• Capacité à analyser les besoins des projets et à proposer des solutions adaptées.
• Connaissance des méthodologies de développement logiciel.
Profil requis :
• Être titulaire d’un diplôme d’ingénieur, ou équivalent, relevant du développement informatique ou similaire
(Diplôme donnant accès à l'échelle 11 de la Fonction Publique) ;
• Justifier d’une expérience professionnelle cumulée d’une année minimum en développement
informatique;
• Maitriser parfaitement les langages et les Frameworks de développement full stack (FrontEnd ; BackEnd ;
Python, PHP/Laravel, Java/SpringBoot) ;
• Maitriser les techniques et approches de conception des applications ;
• Maitriser les méthodes Agiles de gestion de projet informatique ;
• Maîtriser la gestion des bases de données ;
• Maitriser la rédaction du plan de test (test fonctionnels, tests d’intégration, tests de non-régression, tests
techniques) pour chaque sprint de l’application ;
• Maitriser l’automatisation des tests ;
• Posséder des compétences en développement RV/RA ou Mobile serait un plus significatif ;
• Être âgé de moins de 45 ans à la date de la prise de service ;
• Être de nationalité Marocaine.

Dossier de candidature :
• Formulaire de candidature (F1) à renseigner (Format PDF), téléchargeable depuis le site www.ofppt.ma;
• CV actualisé et explicitant de manière détaillée les expériences professionnelles en rapport avec le poste
(Format PDF) ;
• Copie du diplôme requis (les diplômes délivrés par les établissements étrangers doivent être
accompagnés par des copies des attestations d’équivalence) (Format PDF) ;
• Copie de la CNI (Recto-verso) en Format PDF (Une seule page).
Modalités de dépôt de dossier de candidature :
S’inscrire et Postuler en envoyant le dossier de candidature sous format PDF à l’offre sur le site :
http://recrutement.ofppt.ma ;
Date limite de réception des candidatures est le 18 Octobre 2026 à minuit.
N.B : Tout dossier incomplet ou transmis via un canal autre que celui précité ne sera pas pris en
considération.
Toute information erronée entrainera l’annulation du dossier de candidature.
Date et lieu du concours :
Les candidats présélectionnés sur dossier seront convoqués à des tests d’évaluation, dont les dates et les
lieux de déroulement seront indiqués ultérieurement.
Affectation :

job_document_texts.text:
Référence _ Annonce : RH 105/26
L’Office de la Formation Professionnelle et de la Promotion du Travail
lance un Appel à Candidatures pour le poste de :
Formateur en développement digital
(Nombre de Postes : 05)
Descriptif de poste :
Le formateur en développement digital joue un rôle essentiel dans la formation d'une nouvelle génération de
professionnels compétents dans ce domaine en constante évolution, et sa contribution est cruciale pour
répondre aux besoins du marché du travail dans le secteur des nouvelles technologies de l'information.
Le formateur en développement digital occupe un rôle crucial dans le développement des compétences des
stagiaires dans le domaine du développement des nouvelles technologies de l'information. Son objectif
principal est de former une nouvelle génération de professionnels compétents dans le domaine du
développement numérique en leur fournissant les connaissances théoriques et pratiques nécessaires pour
réussir dans ce domaine en constante évolution.
Responsabilités :
• Analyser et interpréter les cahiers des charges pour comprendre les besoins des projets de développement
digital.
• Rédiger des spécifications fonctionnelles et techniques détaillées pour guider le processus de
développement.
• Concevoir et réaliser des maquettes et des prototypes pour visualiser et valider les concepts proposés.
• Concevoir et mettre en place des bases de données pour stocker et gérer efficacement les données.
• Développer des composants logiciels à l'aide de langages de programmation orientés objet tels que Java,
C#, Python, etc.
• Assembler et intégrer les différents composants logiciels pour créer des applications fonctionnelles.
• Réaliser des tests unitaires et des tests d'intégration pour garantir la qualité et la fiabilité des applications
développées.
• Participer à la mise en exploitation des applications et fournir un support technique aux utilisateurs finaux.
• Assurer une veille technologique constante pour rester à jour avec les dernières tendances et technologies
en développement digital.
Compétences requises :
• Excellentes compétences en communication pour transmettre efficacement les connaissances aux
stagiaires.
• Solide expérience pratique dans le développement de logiciels et d'applications digitales.
• Maîtrise des langages de programmation orientés objet et des frameworks associés.
• Capacité à travailler de manière autonome et en équipe.
• Compétences organisationnelles pour planifier et dispenser efficacement les formations.
• Capacité à analyser les besoins des projets et à proposer des solutions adaptées.
• Connaissance des méthodologies de développement logiciel.
Profil requis :
• Être titulaire d’un diplôme d’ingénieur, ou équivalent, relevant du développement informatique ou similaire
(Diplôme donnant accès à l'échelle 11 de la Fonction Publique) ;
• Justifier d’une expérience professionnelle cumulée d’une année minimum en développement
informatique;
• Maitriser parfaitement les langages et les Frameworks de développement full stack (FrontEnd ; BackEnd ;
Python, PHP/Laravel, Java/SpringBoot) ;
• Maitriser les techniques et approches de conception des applications ;
• Maitriser les méthodes Agiles de gestion de projet informatique ;
• Maîtriser la gestion des bases de données ;
• Maitriser la rédaction du plan de test (test fonctionnels, tests d’intégration, tests de non-régression, tests
techniques) pour chaque sprint de l’application ;
• Maitriser l’automatisation des tests ;
• Posséder des compétences en développement RV/RA ou Mobile serait un plus significatif ;
• Être âgé de moins de 45 ans à la date de la prise de service ;
• Être de nationalité Marocaine.

Dossier de candidature :
• Formulaire de candidature (F1) à renseigner (Format PDF), téléchargeable depuis le site www.ofppt.ma;
• CV actualisé et explicitant de manière détaillée les expériences professionnelles en rapport avec le poste
(Format PDF) ;
• Copie du diplôme requis (les diplômes délivrés par les établissements étrangers doivent être
accompagnés par des copies des attestations d’équivalence) (Format PDF) ;
• Copie de la CNI (Recto-verso) en Format PDF (Une seule page).
Modalités de dépôt de dossier de candidature :
S’inscrire et Postuler en envoyant le dossier de candidature sous format PDF à l’offre sur le site :
http://recrutement.ofppt.ma ;
Date limite de réception des candidatures est le 18 Octobre 2026 à minuit.
N.B : Tout dossier incomplet ou transmis via un canal autre que celui précité ne sera pas pris en
considération.
Toute information erronée entrainera l’annulation du dossier de candidature.
Date et lieu du concours :
Les candidats présélectionnés sur dossier seront convoqués à des tests d’évaluation, dont les dates et les
lieux de déroulement seront indiqués ultérieurement.
Affectation :
Errachidia.

articles.job_description: خيارات الوصول المرئي متصرف من الدرجة الثالثة - سُلمْ 10 الإدارة المنظمة مكتب تنمية التعاون آخر أجل لإيداع الترشيحات 16 أكتوبر 2026 - 16:30 تاريخ إجراء المباراة 22 نونبر 2026 تاريخ النشر 1 أكتوبر 2026 معلومات عن المباراة الدرجة : متصرف من الدرجة الثالثة - سُلمْ 10 نوع الإيداع : الإيداع الإلكتروني على الموقع المخصص للإدارة موقع الإيداع : https://www.odco.gov.ma/e-recrutement معلومات إضافية : ترفض طلبات الترشيح غير المسجلة إلكترونيا، وكل ترشيح غيــــر مستوف للوثائق السالفة الذكر أو تم تحميله بطريقة غيـــر صحيحة أو خـــــارج الآجــــــــال لن يــــــؤخـــذ بعــــــيــــــــن الاعتبـــــــار ويحتفظ به دون جواب. سيتم الإعــــــلان عن مكان إجراء المباراة ولائحة المترشحين المقبولين لاجتياز الاختبارات الكتابية والشفوية وكذلك النتائج النهائية للمباراة على الموقع الالكتروني لمكتب تنمية التعاون www.odco.gov.ma وعلى بوابة التشغيل العمومي www.emploi-public.ma. ويعتبر ذلك بمثابة استدعاء للمترشحين المعنيين. هذا الفضاء مخصص لطرح الأسئلة والاستفسارات فقط، وليس لإيداع ملفات الترشيح. تأكيد بواسطة البريد الالكتروني تم إرسال رسالة لتأكيد تسجيل حسابك. يرجى التحقق من رسائل البريد الإلكتروني الخاصة بك

ai_input_package.title: مباريات التوظيف : متصرف من الدرجة الثالثة - سُلمْ 10
ai_input_package.content_preview: خيارات الوصول المرئي متصرف من الدرجة الثالثة - سُلمْ 10 الإدارة المنظمة مكتب تنمية التعاون آخر أجل لإيداع الترشيحات 16 أكتوبر 2026 - 16:30 تاريخ إجراء المباراة 22 نونبر 2026 تاريخ النشر 1 أكتوبر 2026 معلومات عن المباراة الدرجة : متصرف من الدرجة الثالثة - سُلمْ 10 نوع الإيداع : الإيداع الإلكتروني على الموقع المخصص للإدارة موقع الإيداع : https://www.odco.gov.ma/e-recrutement معلومات إضافية : ترفض طلبات الترشيح غير المسجلة إلكترونيا، وكل ترشيح غيــــر مستوف للوثائق السالفة الذكر أو تم تحميله بطريقة غيـــر صحيحة أو خـــــارج الآجــــــــال لن يــــــؤخـــذ بعــــــيــــــــن الاعتبـــــــار ويحتفظ به دون جواب. سيتم الإعــــــلان عن مكان إجراء المباراة ولائحة المترشحين المقبولين لاجتياز الاختبارات الكتابية والشفوية وكذلك النتائج النهائية للمباراة على الموقع الالكتروني لمكتب تنمية التعاون www.odco.gov.ma وعلى بوابة التشغيل العمومي www.emploi-public.ma. ويعتبر ذلك بمثابة استدعاء للمترشحين المعنيين. هذا الفضاء مخصص لطرح الأسئلة والاستفسارات فقط، وليس لإيداع ملفات الترشيح. تأكيد بواسطة البريد الالكتروني تم إرسال رسالة لتأكيد تسجيل حسابك. يرجى التحقق من رسائل البريد الإلكتروني الخاصة بك
